text:
toni: quick heads-up — noticed aggressive shard prefetch for our "latency-critical" customers is blowing the shared warmup cache during peak.
jasper: ugh, yeah. which policy is triggering full-shard prefetch? the per-request QoS tag or pool-level heuristics?
toni: currently both. qos tag forces aggressive_full_shard=true and pool will top up to 80% warm cache if any tenant is flagged.
rachel: that explains the thrashing. we're making one tenant happy, five others suffer higher cold starts + OOMs.
miguel: can we add a budget cap + admission control? e.g. per-pool warmup_budget and per-tenant emergency override with token accounting.
sam: +1. also we should expose cost attribution so sales/CS can see warmup charges — otherwise month-end surprises.
jasper: sketching a small policy: warmup_budget (fraction of pool memory), qos_priority (int), and prefetch_mode: {aggressive, conservative, incremental}. default conservative.
toni: proposal looks good. conservative should do prefix+kv cache first, fall back to full shards only if sustained tail latency > SLO for X secs.
rachel: how do we detect 'sustained tail latency'? server-side moving-window? we already have per-route p99 histograms in console.
miguel: use moving-window p99 per model-route with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. e.g. window=30s, require 3 consecutive windows > threshold.
sam: role for admission control: if warmup_budget used > 70% then degrade new warmup requests to incremental mode and queue.
toni: edge cases: bursty traffic where incremental won't catch up; maybe allow a one-time fast-path if request is tagged emergency by enterprise SLA (and charge them).
jasper: agree — add a circuit-breaker: if pool free memory < X and other tenants suffering p99 > margin -> deny aggressive warmup.
warmup-bot: bot note: I observed 6 aggressive warmups in pool gpu-pool-03 between 03:02-03:07, causing eviction chatter and 3 OOMs.
ton i: thanks. can you paste the sample config we'd ship in the release? small enough to ship in feature flag.
jasper: here's a minimal flag example:

```
warmup:
  budget_per_pool: 0.06        # fraction of pool mem reserved for warmup
  qos_priority_limits:
    latency-critical: 0.5     # fraction of warmup budget
  prefetch_mode: incremental # conservative default
  emergency_override: true
  hysteresis_windows: 3
  window_seconds: 30
```

rachel: looks reasonable. let's add telemetry: warmup_budget_used, warmup_evictions, warmup_denied_count, p99_affected_tenants.
miguel: will prototype admission controller + metrics in the warmup service PR. aim for opt-in by next week.
toni: timeline OK. SJ (sales) asked for a one-pager on pricing impact if they opt into emergency_full_shard. sam can you draft?
sam: yeah will draft. also recommend we add a billable metric "warmup_bytes" to the usage API.
jasper: one more thing — prefer soft-rollout: per-tenant feature-flag with monitor alarms before global flip.
rachel: ack. I'll add alarm dashboards and an auto rollback playbook if p99 regression > 5%.
warmup-bot: deploy-bot: warmup-service/pr-3425 merged to staging. running canary on gpu-pool-03 for 10m.
toni: thanks all. follow-up: if canary stable, open a RFC-lite to make prefetch_mode a first-class field in model manifest.
sam: noted.
